question: When estate agents valued a house after seeing its list price, what set them apart from amateurs?
answer: Not their accuracy but their denial. In Northcraft and Neale's study, agents who toured the same house valued it higher when handed a higher list price, much as students did. The students admitted the list price had swayed them; most agents said they had ignored it. The anchor worked on people sure it had not.
move: Feeling unmoved by a number is no evidence that it did not move you.
ask: Which number do I swear didn't affect me, only because I don't feel it did?
reference: Northcraft & Neale, Experts, Amateurs, and Real Estate: An Anchoring-and-Adjustment Perspective on Property Pricing Decisions, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1987
